title: Stagecoach Interior
description: A heavy carriage that smells of old leather and anxious sweat, lurching violently over the rutted track. Through the front partition, the Caretaker can be heard whipping the two panicked horses, his manic muttering competing with the groan of straining axles. The interior lanterns sway wildly, casting erratic shadows that offer no comfort against the encroaching dark.
summary: The cramping interior of a heavy carriage where the Caretaker drives two panicked horses down the rutted track.

title: Crash Site
description: A muddy depression in the road where the carriage's axle finally gave way to the rough terrain. The vehicle lies crippled on its side, spilling trunks and provisions into the mire while the horses have torn free of their traces and vanished. The driver is nowhere to be seen, leaving the survivors alone beneath the looming, hostile boughs.
summary: A muddy depression where the carriage lies crippled, spilling provisions into the mire after the horses tore free.

title: Prologue Old Road
description: A narrow, rutted track cutting through ancient woodland, where the ground rises and falls in slow, indifferent waves. The road is bordered by leaning stones and half-swallowed marker posts, their carvings worn smooth by weather and neglect. Here the forest feels not merely wild but watchful: crows shift on high branches, and the undergrowth holds its breath when footsteps approach. Fog clings low to the ditches, and the air smells of wet bark, cold iron, and old rot. The Hamlet lies ahead somewhere beyond the trees, but the road offers no sign of it—only the sense that each step forward is another step deeper into a place that remembers.
summary: A rutted woodland track of fog, old markers, and watchful silence, leading toward a Hamlet still out of sight.
